corrected_content.problem:
Which of the following is equivalent to the integral $$
\displaystyle \int_(C)(x^{3} - y)ds,
$$ where the curve $C$ is parametrized by $\mathbf{r}(t)=2t\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{i}+(2-t)\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{j}\hspace{0.167em}$ for $-1 \le t \le 2$?
corrected_content.worked_solution: Substitute $x=2t$, $y=2-t$ to get $x^3-y=8t^3+t-2$. The speed is $\sqrt{2^2+(-1)^2}=\sqrt5$. Therefore $$\int_C(x^3-y)\,ds=\sqrt5\int_{-1}^{2}(8t^3+t-2)\,dt.$$
